questions.question: As per November 2022, who is the Chief Economic Advisor of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __V Anantha Nageswaran__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• V Anantha Nageswaran

 
 
• A renowned economist with a focus on academia is Dr. Venkatraman Anantha Nageswaran.
 
• In 1985, Nageswaran earned a post-graduate diploma in management (MBA) from the Indian Institute of Management (IIM), Ahmedabad.
 
• He later earned a doctorate in 1994 for his research on the empirical behaviour of exchange rates from the University of Massachusetts Amherst.
 
• Between 1994 and 2011, he held a number of executive positions in macroeconomic and capital market research for several private wealth management companies in Switzerland and Singapore.
 
• The Indian government has appointer Dr. Venkatraman Anantha Nageswaran as its Chief Economic Adviser (CEA) in January 2022.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Chief Economic Advisor (CEA) of India

 
 
• A position in the Indian government known as the Chief Economic Adviser (CEA) is equivalent to that of a secretary in that government.
 
• The Indian Economic Service's ex-officio cadre controlling authority is the CEA.
 
• The CEA is the director of the Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance, Government of India.
 
• The CEA job was a Union Public Service Commission appointment until 2009, and up until the 1970s, the majority of CEAs were employees of the Indian Economic Service.
 
• The Economic Survey, which presents the government's annual economic performance and recommendations for potential reforms, is the key role played by the CEA.

questions.question: Who sworn in as the 49th Chief Justice of India in August 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Uday Umesh Lalit__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• President Droupadi Murmu has appointed Justice Uday Umesh Lalit as the** 49th Chief Justice of India (CJI).**
 
• He will succeed Justice N V Ramana, who will retire on **26 August 2022.**
 
• Justice Lalit was appointed a judge of the Supreme Court in 2014.
 
• He will become the second CJI to be directly elevated to the Supreme Court from the Bar, after Justice S.M. Sikri, who served as the 13th CJI in 1971.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Supreme Court:

 
 
• ​The Supreme Court of India is the highest judicial court and the final court of appeal under the Constitution of India.
 
• It is also the highest constitutional court, with the power of judicial review.
 
• India is a federal State and has a single and unified judicial system with a three-tier structure.
 
• The Indian constitution provides for a provision of the Supreme Court under Part V (The Union) and Chapter 6 (The Union Judiciary).
 
• Articles 124 to 147 in Part V of the Constitution deal with the organisation, independence, jurisdiction, powers and procedures of the Supreme Court.
 
• The promulgation of Regulating Act of 1773 established the Supreme Court of Judicature at Calcutta as a Court of Record, with full power & authority.
 
• It was established to hear and determine all complaints for any crimes and also to entertain, hear and determine any suits or actions in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.
 
• The Supreme Courts at Madras and Bombay were established by King George – III in 1800 and 1823 respectively.
 
 
 
• In Oct 2022 D Y Chandrachud has been Appointed as the 50th Chief Justice Of India.

questions.question: Which among the following metals has the highest electrical conductivity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Silver**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The metal with the** highest electrical conductivity** among the options given is **Silver**.
 
• Here are a few points explaining this:
 
• **Conductivity:**
 
 
• **​**Silver has the highest electrical conductivity of all elements.
 
• It's used in many industrial applications because of this property.
 
 
 
• **Resistance to Corrosion:**
 
 
• **​**Despite being highly conductive, silver isn't always the first choice for an electrical conductor in practical applications because it tarnishes and corrodes more easily than some other metals.
 
 
 
• **Cost:**
 
 
• **​**Silver is more expensive than many other materials.
 
• Copper, while not as conductive, is used more frequently because it's less expensive.
 
 
 
• **Heat Sensitivity:**
 
 
• **​**Silver's conductivity decreases as it gets hotter, so it's not ideal for high-temperature applications.
 
 
 
• **Malleability and Ductility:**
 
 
• **​**Silver is malleable and ductile, making it easier to draw into wires for electrical applications.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• This significant event marks the official start of the Games.
 
• **Naomi Osaka, at the time, was one of the most notable athletes in the world.**
 
• **The Olympic cauldron symbolizes the official start of the Olympic Games.**
 
• The tradition of lighting the cauldron comes from the ancient **Greek Olympic Games, where a flame was kept burning throughout the duration of the event.**

• The Olympics took place in Tokyo.
 
• The cauldron was held by Naomi Osaka.
 
• Its mascots were Miraitowa (official mascot of the 2020 Summer Olympics) and Someity (the official mascot of the 2020 Summer Paralympics).
 
 
• The United States topped the medal tally of Summer Olympics 2021 with 39 golds.
 
• The People's Republic of China stood in second place with a total of 38 gold medals.
 
• And Japan was third with a total of 27.
 
• India's rank in the summer Olympic 2021 was 48th.
 
 
 
 
 
• Olympics:
 
 
• Athens was the venue for the first Olympics which was held in 1896.

• The Olympic motto is “*Citius Altius Fortius*” (faster, higher, stronger).

questions.question: Neonatal mortality rate refers to the number of deaths during the first ________ of life per 1000 live births in a given year or other period.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**28 days**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The number of deaths during the first 28 completed days of life per 1000 live births in a given year or period is defined as the neonatal mortality rate.
 
• There are some concerns about the quality of neonatal mortality reporting both internationally and within states, particularly in terms of defining a live birth and/or reporting both birth and death certificates for newborns with very low birth weights.
 
• When neonatal death certificates are matched to corresponding birth certificates, much more additional and valuable data (birth weight, mother's smoking status, when prenatal care began, etc.) is obtained for neonatal mortality risk analysis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The number of newborn deaths per 1,000 live births is known as **t**he infant mortality rate.
 
• The infant mortality rate is an essential indicator of a society's general health, in addition to providing crucial information regarding maternal and baby health.
 
• The crude mortality rate is derived by dividing the number of fatalities in a particular time by the number of people who were at risk of dying during that period.
 
• A death rate that is limited to a certain age group is known as an age-specific mortality rate.

questions.question: Which of the following comes under Mollusca?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Octopus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Kingdom- Animalia 
 
• Phylum- Mollusca
 
• Class- Cephalopoda
 
• Genus- Octopus
 
• Octopus belongs to the class Cephalopoda.
 
• Octopuses have three hearts; a systemic heart that circulates blood around the body and two branchial hearts that pump it through each of the two gills.
 
• The systemic heart is inactive when the animal is swimming and thus it tires quickly and prefers to crawl.
 
• Octopus blood contains the copper-rich protein hemocyanin to transport oxygen.
 
• This makes the blood very viscous and it requires considerable pressure to pump it around the body.
 
• Octopus's blood pressures can exceed 75 mmHg.
 
• All octopuses are venomous, evidence shows that the animal does not make the venom by itself, but is produced by symbiotic bacteria instead.
 
• The blue-ringed octopus is the most venomous to humans and they are fatal.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The five-kingdom system proposed by R.H. Whittaker.
 
• The kingdom defined by him was named- Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia.
 
• Kingdom Animalia is divided into sub-groups which is known as Phylum. There are 11 phyla in the kingdom Animalia.
 
 
• Porifera, Coelenterata, Ctenophora, Platyhelminthes, Aschelminthes, Annelida, Arthropoda, Mollusca, Echinodermata, Hemichordata, Chordata.

questions.question: General Dyer took command during the martial law in which year?
questions.solution:

__
 
• Martial law was imposed in India during the command of General Dyer. 
 
• On April 13, 1919, General Dyer signed the Martial Law Act, which stated that no more than two people might establish a group and congregate in one location.
 
• This law was passed to prohibit any organised opposition to the reigning powers.
 
• This occurred during the Sikh festival of Baisakhi when hundreds had congregated in Jallianwala Bagh to celebrate, and General Dyer opened fire on them.
 
• Except for Article 34, which gives Parliament the ability to reimburse persons for crimes committed in regions where martial law was in effect and to recognise acts committed under martial law, there is no explicit mention of "martial law" in the Indian Constitution.

• Preventive detention is the practice of incarcerating accused individuals before trial on the idea that their release would be detrimental to society—specifically, that they would be more likely to commit new crimes if released.

questions.question: What helps in expanding trade and commerce and brings in foreign exchange?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**export of manufactured goods**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **export of manufactured goods **involves selling domestically produced goods to foreign markets, driving economic growth, and generating employment.
 
• However, it comes with challenges like trade **barriers, international competition, and quality control**.
 
• Strategies to increase exports include improving produc**t quality, exploring new markets, and seeking government support**.
 
• The export of manufactured goods is a key indicator of a **country's economic health and industrial strength**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Expanding trade and commerce** 

 
 
• Expanding trade and commerce involves increasing the exchange of goods, services, and capital across** international borders**.
 
• This process helps diversify domestic economies, promotes economic growth, and **leads to the creation of jobs**.
 
• Bringing in foreign exchange refers to earning foreign currencies through **exports or foreign investments**.
 
• This is crucial for a country as it allows it to pay for its imports, repay foreign loans, and conduct other **international transactions**.

questions.question: Which of the following archaeological sites is NOT located in present day India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mehrgarh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mehrgarh (6500 to 5500 BC) is one of the oldest Neolithic sites in South Asia.
 
• It began during the Pre-Harappan period.
 
• It is located near the Bolan Pass on the Kacchi Plain of Balochistan, Pakistan.
 
• It is one of the earliest sites with evidence of farming and herding.
 
• Women and men learnt to grow barley and wheat, and rear sheep and goats.
 
• Remains of square or rectangular houses were found at the site.
 
• These people believe in life after death, this was visible from the burials which were found at the site.

• 
 The Indus Valley Civilization or Harappan Civilization was a Bronze Age civilization.
 
 
• 
 The Indus Valley Civilization was established around 3300 BC.
 
 
• 
 It flourished between 2600 BC and 1900 BC (Mature Indus Valley Civilization) around river Indus and its tributaries.
 
 
• 
 It started declining around 1900 BC and disappeared around 1400 BC.
 
 
• 
 This is also called Harappan Civilization after the first city to be excavated, Harappa (Punjab, Pakistan).
 
 
• 
 The Harappan Civilization was a contemporary of Egyptian Civilization.
 
 
• 
 The Egyptian Civilization was also a Bronze Age civilization which developed along the banks of river Nile.
 
 
• 
 
The Egyptian Civilization lasted for over 3000 years from 3150 BCE to 30 BCE.
